supportingContinuities: manga and other official materials may be indexed as separately named variants
analysisLayers: RM97 explanation blog is retained as analysis-derived and never silently promoted to primary canon

entities.name: Altair
entities.summary: Setsuna Shimazaki's secondary creation based on Shirotsumekusa. Altair is an independent existence without a fixed originating story and is responsible for bringing Created characters into the Real World.

entities.name: Setsuna Shimazaki
entities.summary: Altair's creator and Sōta Mizushino's former friend; her death is central to Altair's motive and the series' final resolution.

entities.name: Sōta Mizushino
entities.summary: A high-school student and aspiring creator whose relationship with Setsuna and later intervention become central to the conflict.

entities.name: Sirius
entities.summary: A creator-built counter to Altair with a closely matched power set but insufficiently developed identity, allowing Altair to take control after their confrontation.

entities.name: Created
entities.summary: Fictional characters who emerge into the Real World; once there they can act beyond some of the plot-bound emotional constraints of their home stories.

mechanics.name: Audience Acceptance
mechanics.summary: Audience acceptance determines whether revisions, creations, or added abilities can be sustained. Arcsweep stores RM97's expanded mechanics discussion separately as analysis-derived.

mechanics.name: Holopsicon
mechanics.summary: Altair's evolving repertoire. Canon sources attribute world transition/transport, telekinesis, flight, defensive sword formations, deletion or erasure effects, story revision and further abilities arising from accepted derivative portrayals.

mechanics.name: Narrative causality
mechanics.summary: Storyworld characters originate inside authored causal structures; manifestation into the Real World changes the degree to which those structures bind their choices.

mechanics.name: Restorative Power of the Real World
mechanics.summary: RM97's mechanics index uses this label for the Real World's tendency to reject or normalise anomalous manifested elements. It remains an analytical vocabulary item pending primary-source anchoring.

events.name: Great Destruction
events.summary: Altair's plan to make worlds collide and destroy the rationality of the Real World in vengeance for Setsuna.

events.name: Birdcage / Elimination Chamber Festival
events.summary: A live creator-authored crossover confrontation designed to constrain Altair and use audience acceptance to support countermeasures.

events.name: Altair versus Sirius
events.summary: Sirius temporarily overcomes Altair, but Altair returns and takes control because Sirius lacks a sufficiently established personality/identity.

events.name: Setsuna resolution
events.summary: The final confrontation returns Setsuna to Altair; Altair ultimately creates a new world for them, with reciprocal creator/created authorship imagery.

antiFlattening: Do not turn frame manipulation into detached commentary.
Do not confuse identical powers with identical identity.
Do not erase Altair's capacity to refuse, deceive, negotiate, or change the encounter's premise.

revisionNotes: Primary canon and secondary mechanics analysis remain separately labelled.
No source prose is mirrored wholesale; records are compact paraphrased canon/index data.
